input.question: Does eating dirt as a child have any proven benefits for your immune system?
input.ground_truth: Not so much a boosted immune system, but polio affected the upper and middle class far worse than the lower class because kids were exposed to the virus early on in low income areas. As a consequence they became immune to it, while the upper class kids were exposed later in life when it had a far more deleterious effect. [source](_URL_0_)

Question: Does eating dirt as a child have any proven benefits for your immune system?

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you’re asking about eating a tiny bit of dirt, like what happens if you accidentally get some on your hands and then touch your mouth.

Some people think that eating a little bit of dirt when you’re a kid might help your body learn how to fight germs, because there are tiny things in dirt that your body can practice with. But scientists have not found any real proof that eating dirt is good for you. In fact, eating dirt can make you sick because it can have bad germs and yucky things in it.

So, it’s better to wash your hands and not eat dirt, even if you think it might help your body get strong. Your body learns to fight germs in other, safer ways!
